dct_creator_sm: Mortezapour, Marzieh (Simon Fraser University). ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5140-5003
dct_description_sm:
This dataset contains global climate model outputs generated using the CanESM5.1 Earth
system model to investigate the hydrological and biogeophysical impacts of reforestation
under different land-cover scenarios. The dataset spans a historical simulation period
(1850–2014) and future projections (2015–2200) under the SSP1-2.6 emissions scenario. This
enables long-term analysis of land-use-driven changes in climate and hydrology. The
simulations were designed to isolate the effects of land-cover change by holding
atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations constant across scenarios, ensuring that
differences in climate variables arise from biogeophysical processes rather than radiative
forcing.

The dataset includes four main components corresponding to different simulation scenarios:
a historical baseline, a future baseline scenario with constant land cover, a sustainable
reforestation scenario, and a reversed reforestation scenario. Each scenario is
represented by five ensemble members, generated through perturbations in ocean initial
conditions to capture internal climate variability . We provide the data in NetCDF format
and include key hydrological and energy balance variables such as near-surface air
temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration, soil moisture, runoff, cloud fraction, and
radiative fluxes.
